name: Royal Ring
sourceText: 1 carrot

name: Royal Coat
sourceText: 2 carrots

name: Royal Scepter
sourceText: 3 carrots

name: Royal Chalice
sourceText: 4 carrots

name: Royal Crown
sourceText: 5 carrots

name: Royal Carrot
sourceText: 6 carrots

name: Left Glove
sourceText: 1 carrot alone; if you also have Right Glove, each glove is worth 4 → 8 total

name: Right Glove
sourceText: same as Left Glove
notes: The source abbreviates this as the same as Left Glove; the reciprocal pairing is made explicit using rulebook page 11.

name: Bureaucrat
sourceText: 1 carrot for each Parchment you own, including this one

name: Burgomaster
sourceText: 1 carrot per City
notes: Count cities, not their towers/strength (rulebook page 10).

name: Diplomat
sourceText: 1 carrot per territory you control along the outside edge of the board
notes: Count a controlled border territory once, including corners. Border and corner definitions here refer to the original rectangular board.

name: Explorer
sourceText: 3 carrots per corner territory you control
notes: The original board corners are A1, A10, J1, and J10.

name: Carpenter
sourceText: 1 carrot per Wood resource you produce

name: Master Carpenter
sourceText: 2 carrots per Wood resource

name: Woodland King
sourceText: 20 carrots if you produce at least 7 Wood

name: Fisher
sourceText: 1 carrot per Fish resource you produce

name: Master Fisher
sourceText: 2 carrots per Fish resource

name: Fisher King
sourceText: 20 carrots if you produce at least 7 Fish

name: Farmer
sourceText: 1 carrot per Carrot resource you produce

name: Master Farmer
sourceText: 2 carrots per Carrot resource

name: Carrot King
sourceText: 15 carrots if you produce at least 5 Carrots

name: Merchant
sourceText: 3 carrots per Luxury Resource you produce
notes: Count luxury-resource production, including farms; basic carrots and the field luxury resource remain distinct.

name: Master of the Mountains
sourceText: 2 carrots per Mountain territory you control

name: Carrotistador
sourceText: 4 carrots for every Fief containing at least 3 territories

name: Harecingetorix
sourceText: 1 carrot per Fief you control

name: Hun-ny King
sourceText: 12 carrots if you have at least 10 Fiefs

name: Bun-Shee
sourceText: 2 carrots per City in your Fiefs that produce no resources
notes: Check resource production across the entire fief, then count its cities, regardless of city strength.

name: PanPan the Barbarian
sourceText: 2 carrots per territory you control that has neither a City nor a resource
notes: Check each territory separately. A city or resource elsewhere in the fief does not disqualify it. A Camp or Sky Tower is not a city (rulebook page 11).

name: Colonist
sourceText: 3 carrots for each Camp card you played
notes: The supplied text counts Camp cards played, not Camp tokens currently on the board. Keep card-play history separate from surviving camps; this is a transcription of the supplied summary.

name: King of Thieves
sourceText: 12 carrots if you have at least 9 Cities

name: Matriarch
sourceText: 12 carrots if you control the most territories
notes: The tie policy is deliberately unset pending a verified clarification.

name: Little Prince
sourceText: perform another harvest of all your Fiefs except your best Fief
notes: If multiple fiefs tie for highest harvest, exclude exactly one of them (rulebook page 11).

name: Treasure Guardian
sourceText: 3 carrots for each Treasure Parchment you own
notes: A copied treasure qualifies for this bonus (rulebook page 11).

name: Treasure Hunter
sourceText: doubles the value of your Treasure Parchments
notes: Copied treasures qualify. This effect changes treasure values; it must not be counted as an unrelated fixed-point reward. Stacking with a copied Hunter remains open.

name: Liberal
sourceText: copy one Parchment belonging to the player on your right
notes: Copy the whole card. A copied treasure qualifies for Treasure Guardian and Treasure Hunter bonuses (rulebook page 11).

name: Socialist
sourceText: copy one Parchment belonging to the player on your left
notes: Copy the whole card. A copied treasure qualifies for Treasure Guardian and Treasure Hunter bonuses (rulebook page 11).

name: Opportunist
sourceText: 10 carrots if you're in second place after final scoring
notes: The user confirmed 10 Golden Carrots for second place after final scoring. The tie policy and interactions between copied Opportunists remain unresolved.
